summary: Aroostook County, ME: wood lookout from 1914, 36-foot steel tower built 1919 and removed in 1993 per Maine Memory; the FFLA list still shows it standing.

facts.design: 36-foot steel tower built in 1919; wood and log-crib lookouts stood on the mountain before it
facts.status_note: The 36-foot steel tower was removed in 1993, according to Maine Memory; the FFLA list still shows a standing tower.

access.note: No current access rules, owner or visiting guidance found in the sources read

corrections.why: Maine Memory's record and the Maine Memory slide, credited to the Maine Forest Service, both say the 36-foot steel tower was removed in 1993. Only the FFLA list still shows a standing tower, and it gives no date or photo.

notes_for_editor: The main conflict is current status: the FFLA list says Standing, while Maine Memory and its exhibit say the 36-foot steel tower was removed in 1993. Facts record status gone with the conflict in the status note, and the corrections list proposes standing to gone for human review; a recent photo or Forest Service record would settle it. The township is TD R2 WELS in Maine Memory and Township 9, Range 3 in the 1914 report; the FFLA coordinates were not checked against either, and the sources do not reconcile the two. Only the 1916 forest commissioner's report, as quoted by Forest Lookouts, calls the site No. 9 or Bald Mountain. Forest Lookouts gives the 1915 replacement as a log crib tower, but the Maine Memory caption says it was a wood tower, and the sources do not settle which. No access source was found, so access is unknown. The Facebook posts about this site were not read. Maine Memory photos 19126 (ca. 1918) and 19127 (ca. 1920) are candidates, but their licence was not checked, so no photo is added.
